answer.new_consideration: The author asks for the maintenance reading of th_maintenance to be reconsidered against its recovered wording (E91 baseline, E92 proposed) and against the declined-share link proposal (E2). The request supplies no criticism to assess.
answer.reconsidered_judgment: Corrected. The reading said the rota carries channel repair and return labour; the record does not say that. E91 and E92 (identical summary text, no changed fields) state that from Book 20 lineage crews carry channel repair under a Special Draw Right, and that households able to meet the rota carry the rest. Old lineages hold the repair skill from Books 9-11. The proposal leaves th_maintenance as it is, so the thread states no change to who performs the labour. E2 changes only the channel: unkept water goes into the refuser's own holding, and its fields and well flood when it stops tending its branch. The conditional consequence stands, qualified: the record states the rota's allocation rule, but not that a flood reduces a household's labour.
answer.creative_significance: Under the selected alternative, refusal costs the refuser its own fields and well when it stops tending its branch (E2). That is a recorded consequence, not a change to labour, and the record leaves open whether it affects the refuser's place on the rota.
